symptom: A new lint rule that reads the MODEL rather than the catalog reports Mendix's own platform content. MPR016's first run on testdata/pedapp reported "41 entities overlap each other on the System domain model diagram: ConsumedODataConfiguration, Error, FileDocument, HttpHeader, HttpMessage, HttpRequest and 35 more" — a model no user can edit (`mxcli layout` refuses System outright). The project's own modules were clean.
cause: Catalog-backed rules get the platform filter for free: every ctx.Entities()/Pages()/... query ends in notPlatformModule(alias) (mdl/linter/context.go), which is `COALESCE(Source,'')='' AND COALESCE(Id,'')<>'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'`. A rule reading the model through the reader (here ListDomainModels, for entity Location, which the catalog does not hold) never passes through that WHERE clause, so it starts out seeing System and every Marketplace module. Fixed by adding LintContext.OwnedModuleNamesByID, the Go counterpart of notPlatformModule, and keying the rule's module resolution on it.
insight: The platform filter lives in the SQL, so it protects only rules that ask the catalog. Any rule needing geometry, an expression or anything else the catalog does not carry must re-apply it in Go, and every such rule starts out broken in exactly this way — QUAL002 shipped it once on these same entities, and MPR016 reproduced it three months later. Two cheap discriminators: run the new rule next to a catalog-based rule with a similar threshold (MPR003 caps a module at 15 persistent entities and reported NOTHING on the same 41-entity System module, which localises the difference to the data source in one step), and read the finding's own entity names — FileDocument and HttpRequest are Mendix's, not any app's. Do NOT reach for modules.Source to fix it: Source is empty for System exactly as for the user's own modules, which is the trap the ID test exists for. Rules reading the model are about to become common (an attribute read-but-never-written check, a model-name-in-a-string-literal check and an index check all need the model), so the helper is the fix rather than a filter per rule.
